newsitem.title: CHINA: Sino-Japan air conditioner venture started.
newsitem.headline: Sino-Japan air conditioner venture started.

text.p: A $40 million automobile air conditioner joint venture between China and Japan has gone into operation in eastern China, the Business Weekly said on Sunday.

The Yantai Shougang Denso Co Ltd, a joint venture between Japan's Denso Corp, Toyoda Automatic Loom Works, Toyota Tsusho and China's Shougang Iron and Steel Group, had gone into production in early November, the newspaper said.
The Chinese and Japanese sides had each invested $20 million in the project in Yantai in the eastern province of Shandong, the newspaper said without giving further details.
The new venture had a production capacity of 180,000 air conditioners a year and aimed to generate 1.44 billion yuan ($173 million) in annual sales, it said.

The shareholders were planning to invest another $20 million in the venture to boost output capacity to 360,000 units a year and sales to 2.88 billion yuan ($347 million) a year, the newspaper said without giving a timetable.
The venture's products would be sold to domestic auto firms as well as exported to Southeast Asia, it said.
Yantai Shougang Denso had adopted refrigeration compression and non-freon cooling technologies from automobile air conditioner firm Denso, it said.
